verses.1: The lord of Rakshasas, Ravana, having been crowned and accompanied by his two brothers, then thought about giving his Rakshasi sister in marriage.
verses.2: He gave his Rakshasi sister, named Surpanakha, to Vidyujjihva, who was a lord among the Danavas of the Kalakeya clan.
verses.3: Then, Ravana himself, having given (leave to others), wandered for hunting, and there, O Rama, he saw Maya, the son of Diti.
verses.4: Seeing him accompanied by a maiden, Ravana, the night-wanderer, asked, "Who are you, alone in this forest devoid of humans and animals, and for what purpose do you stay with this fawn-eyed maiden?"
verses.5: O Rama, Maya thus spoke to the inquiring night-wanderer, "Listen, I shall narrate all that has happened concerning me."
verses.6: O dear one, if you have heard of an Apsara named Hema before, she was given to me by the gods, just as Paulomi was given to Indra.
verses.7: O dear one, I was devoted to her for five hundred years, and she has now been gone for thirteen years for a divine purpose.
verses.8: Then, for the fourteenth year, a golden city, adorned with diamonds and lapis lazuli, was created by me through illusion.
verses.9: There I resided, miserable, deprived of her, and exceedingly sorrowful.
verses.10: Having taken my daughter from that city, I came to the forest; this is my daughter, O King, who grew in her womb.
verses.11: I have come with her to seek a husband for her, for indeed, the fatherhood of a daughter is a sorrow for all who desire honor.
verses.12: Indeed, a daughter always keeps two families in a state of uncertainty; also, two sons were born to me from this wife.
verses.13: O dear one, Mayavi was the first, and Dundubhi came after him; thus, everything has been truthfully told to you who asked.
verses.14: "How shall I know you now, dear one, who are you?" When thus spoken to, that demon humbly replied this.
verses.15: "I am the son of Pulastya, named Dashagriva, and I am the son of Sage Vishrava, who was the third (generation) from Brahma."
verses.16: O Rama, when the king of demons spoke thus, Maya, the Danava, felt joy upon knowing him to be the son of the great sage, and indeed desired to give his daughter to him.
verses.17: Then, Maya, the king of Daityas, having made the king of Rakshasas grasp his daughter's hand with his own, laughed and spoke these words to him.
verses.18: O King, this is my daughter, born of the Apsara Hema, named Mandodari; let her be accepted as your wife.
verses.19: O Rama, Dashagriva indeed said "Agreed" to him, and having kindled a fire there, he performed the marriage ceremony.
verses.20: O Rama, Maya, indeed knowing of the curse from the ascetic regarding Ravana's paternal grandfather's lineage, gave his daughter to him.
verses.21: And he also gave him the supremely wonderful and unfailing spear, obtained through great penance, by which Lakshmana was struck.
verses.22: Thus, the mighty lord of Lanka, Ravana, having taken wives for himself, went to the city and presented two wives to his brothers.
verses.23: Ravana arranged for Vajrajvala, the granddaughter of Virochana, to be Kumbhakarna's wife.
verses.24: Vibhishana obtained as his wife Sarama, the righteous daughter of the great-souled Gandharva king Shailusha.
verses.25: She was born on the bank of Lake Manasa, and at that time, during the rainy season, Lake Manasa was overflowing.
verses.26: And with affection, the mother of that girl cried out, "O lake, do not grow!", and from that incident, she became known as Sarama.
verses.27: Thus, having taken wives, those Rakshasas indeed enjoyed themselves there, approaching their respective wives, just like Gandharvas in the Nandana garden.
verses.28: Mandodari then gave birth to a son named Meghanada, who is known to you all as Indrajit.
verses.29: Indeed, immediately after his birth, Ravana's son, while crying, emitted a tremendous roar resembling a thundercloud.
verses.30: O Raghava, that Lanka was stunned by his roar, and his father himself named him Meghanada.
verses.31: O Rama, he then grew up in Ravana's beautiful inner palace, protected by excellent women, like a fire hidden by wood.
verses.32: Ravana's son was causing great joy to his mother and father. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे द्वादशः सर्गः ।। 12 ।। Thus ends the twelfth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
